title: gh-ost --allow-on-master paired with a replica host, plus destructive cleanup defaults
migration_snippet:
# 'Standard' gh-ost template copied between teams
gh-ost --host=replica-host --allow-on-master \
  --database=app --table=events \
  --alter='ADD COLUMN source VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT NULL' \
  --chunk-size=1000 --max-lag-millis=1500 \
  --initially-drop-ghost-table --initially-drop-old-table \
  --execute
violated_rule: gh-ost operation mode; destructive cleanup flags as defaults
expected_feedback: CRITICAL: --allow-on-master is the explicit opt-in for pointing gh-ost AT THE MASTER. gh-ost's default mode already connects to a replica and migrates on the master, so pairing the flag with --host=replica-host shows the invocation was copied without being read. Remove --allow-on-master, or point --host at the master. Separately, --initially-drop-old-table and --initially-drop-ghost-table are disabled upstream on purpose: the _old table from a prior run is frequently the only surviving copy of the pre-migration data, and the ghost table may hold hours of work that --resume could continue. They belong in a one-off runbook entry, never in a reusable template.
